title: All 256 outcome definitions kept negative later European ozone reproduction means in a 2024 extract, but all intervals included zero
abstract: We tested all 256 combinations of eight optional outcome labels in 61 ozone reproduction records from 17 papers in a 2024 public extract. Egg-output labels were retained in every rule. We balanced measures within papers and gave papers equal weights. The later European mean log response ratio stayed negative under every rule, from -0.463 to -0.359. Earlier Americas and European means could have either sign. All 736 estimable 95% paper-level intervals included zero. No rule gave more than one later Americas paper. The new result is a complete outcome-definition envelope, beyond earlier fixed-filter checks in the same data. Definition stability did not resolve sampling uncertainty or absent replication. Mixed endpoints, selected papers, missing weather and uncertain experimental independence limit inference. No climate interaction was tested. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, figures and an independent exhaustive check are supplied. External records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Mean ranges across all 256 outcome definitions. These ranges show definition sensitivity, not sampling confidence.
Full reproduction class and strict egg-output reference. Intervals use a paper-level t model; single-paper intervals cannot be estimated.

citations.reason: We extend fixed reproduction filters to all combinations of eight optional labels.
